To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The amplitude and latency of the auditory N1/P200 component of the ERP to speech is modulated by the presence of a visual speech cue.

The amplitude and latency of auditory ERP components to spoken stimuli are modulated by visual speech cues in children, and these effects develop in parallel with speech perception skills over childhood.
The effect of visual cues on the amplitude of the auditory ERP response to speech emerges over the course of childhood, while the effect on response latency does not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of audio visual integration for speech perception.
the development of audio visual speech processing in childhood.
the development of audio visual speech integration in children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
audio visual speech perception develops from a stage of being largely auditory driven to being more visually driven over development.
the effect of latency shortening of the N1/P2 is present at 6 years of age, while the effect on amplitude is only evident by 8 years.
the neural mechanisms of audio-visual speech perception are not fully mature until at least 11 years of development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
children are able to make use of visual speech cues in speech perception, and that this ability develops over mid to late child development.
audio-visual speech perception in children is not fully mature until the end of primary school, and this may be due to an incomplete integration of the visual cues into the speech perception system.
the ability to use visual speech cues to enhance speech perception emerges early in childhood, with a later maturation of the ability to use these cues to enhance auditory processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
audio visual speech perception is a more complex process than previously thought, and that the development of the underlying mechanisms is a more protracted process than previously thought.
the ERP technique can provide a useful window on developmental change in speech processing mechanisms.
children are not fully exploiting audio visual speech cues for language processing at age 11, but the neural mechanisms underlying audio visual integration are present by age 6.
